heads.title: Unsubstantiality
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives mainly describe arguments, claims and things as lacking substance; only 'dreamy' and perhaps 'vacuous' could describe a person, and then only in passing.

heads.title: Intrinsicality
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Adjectives like innate, inborn, ingrained, inbred and radical can describe a person's inherent makeup, but most (intrinsic, fundamental, normal, hereditary, inherited) describe qualities of things.

heads.title: Extrinsicality
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Words such as extrinsic, adventitious, incidental, accidental and contingent describe circumstances or origins, not a person's character.

heads.title: Irrelation
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Insular, independent and arbitrary can describe a person's habitual outlook or manner, while most others (unrelated, adrift, alien, outlandish, incommensurable) describe relations between things.

heads.title: Dissimilarity
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Dissimilarity adjectives (unlike, disparate, divergent, dissimilar) describe differences between things, with no real bearing on a person's character.

heads.title: Nonimitation
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Original, creative and inventive can describe a person's mind, but unmatched, unparalleled, unexampled and untranslated describe achievements or things.

heads.title: Quantity
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: These are indefinite quantity words (some, any, a few, more or less) that describe amounts, not people.

heads.title: Smallness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Smallness adjectives describe size, amount and quality of things; only 'sparing' (frugal in habit) could describe a person.

heads.title: Incoherence
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Incoherent, detached, nonadhesive and immiscible describe physical or logical states, while lax, slack and relaxed can describe a person's easygoing habits.

heads.title: Decomposition
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Decomposed, catalytic, solvent and similar words describe chemical or analytic processes and agents, not people.

heads.title: Completeness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Completeness adjectives describe totality of things; thorough and thorough-going can describe a person's habitual diligence, but most do not describe character.

heads.title: Exclusion
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Exclusion adjectives (excluding, inadmissible, not included in) describe classes and rules, not people's character.

heads.title: Order
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Orderly, neat, tidy, methodical, systematic and businesslike readily describe a person's habitual way of acting, as in 'a methodical person'.

heads.title: Disorder
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Disorderly, untidy, slovenly, aimless, desultory and unmethodical readily describe a person's habitual way of acting, though others describe things.

heads.title: Arrangement
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Methodical, orderly and systematic can describe a person, but arranged, embattled and cut and dried describe arrangements and things.

heads.title: Inclusion
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Included, including, inclusive and congener describe membership or classification, not a person's character.

heads.title: Conformity
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Conformity adjectives (usual, ordinary, normal, typical, habitual, naturalized) mostly describe events, things and rules; only 'orderly' or 'well regulated' could describe a person.

heads.title: Unconformity
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Lawless, wanton, wayward-like aberrant, peculiar, informal and arbitrary can describe a person's conduct, but most (anomalous, abnormal, out of tune, teratogenic) describe things.

heads.title: Unity
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Unity adjectives mostly count or single out things, while lonely, solitary and insular can describe a person's temperament or situation.

heads.title: Synchronism
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Synchronism adjectives (simultaneous, coeval, concurrent, isochronous) describe timing of events, not people.

heads.title: Newness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives (new, novel, recent, fresh, virgin, untried) describe things and time rather than a person's character.

heads.title: Oldness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives (old, ancient, venerable, primeval, prehistoric) describe age or antiquity, not temperament.

heads.title: Youth
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Young, youthful and junior describe age, but callow and juvenile can describe a person's immature manner or temperament.

heads.title: Age
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Most adjectives (aged, elderly, senile, gray, hoary) describe age, though mellow can describe a genial temperament.

heads.title: Adolescence
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Adolescent, pubescent and adult describe life stage, while mature, manly and womanly can describe a person's character.

heads.title: Permanence
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Most adjectives (permanent, intact, inviolate, unrepealed) describe things, though persistent and conservative can describe a person's disposition.

heads.title: Changeableness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Fickle, inconstant, restless, erratic, unstable and versatile are standard descriptions of a person's temperament.

heads.title: Stability
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Steadfast, steady, constant and balanced describe a person's firm disposition, though many other words (immutable, durable, valid) describe things.

heads.title: Chance
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives (casual, fortuitous, accidental, random, statistical) describe events and outcomes rather than character.

heads.title: Power
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Powerful, capable and competent describe ability or force, not habitual character or temperament.

heads.title: Impotence
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives (powerless, unable, incompetent, inept, harmless) describe lack of ability or situation, not character.

heads.title: Weakness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Nervous, soft, weak and effeminate can describe a person's character, but most adjectives (flimsy, gimcrack, sapless) describe things.

heads.title: Destruction
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives describe states of ruin or destructive forces applied to things, not a person's character.

heads.title: Agency
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives (operative, effectual, in force, in action) describe working or operation, not a person's character.

heads.title: Physical Energy
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Energetic, active and brisk can describe a person's habitual manner, but most adjectives (intense, caustic, corrosive, virulent) describe things or forces.

heads.title: Physical Inertness
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Passive, sluggish, inactive and dull can describe a person's habitual way of acting, while most others (latent, smoldering, dormant) describe things.

heads.title: Violence
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Vehement, rude, brusque, waspish, impetuous and bluff are common descriptions of a person's temperament.

heads.title: Moderation
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Calm, gentle, temperate, moderate, sober, unruffled and tranquil are typical descriptions of a person's disposition.

heads.title: Influence
heads.class_title: Words expressing abstract relations
heads.reason: Its adjectives (prevailing, prevalent, rife, rampant, in the ascendant) describe the spread or force of things, with only influential or dominant applying to a person.

heads.title: Region
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Territorial, local and regional describe place, while parochial and provincial can describe a narrow-minded character.

heads.title: Location
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Its adjectives describe a thing's position or fixing (placed, moored, rooted, at anchor), with no character sense.

heads.title: Inhabitant
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Its adjectives are mainly nationalities and occupation or residence terms, which describe origin or status rather than character.

heads.title: Abode
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly settlement types, though 'provincial' and 'rustic' can describe a narrow or unsophisticated person and 'cosmopolitan' a worldly one.

heads.title: Littleness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly physical smallness, but 'petty' (small-minded) and 'puny' can describe a person's nature.

heads.title: Shortness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly physical shortness, but 'curt' describes an abrupt manner in a person.

heads.title: Narrowness. Thinness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly thinness and narrowness of bodies or things, but 'narrow' (narrow-minded) and 'close' (stingy) describe people's dispositions.

heads.title: Height
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly physical height, but 'lofty' can mean haughty, a character trait.

heads.title: Shallowness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly physical depth, but 'shallow' and 'superficial' can describe a person's lack of depth of mind.

heads.title: Verticality
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly orientation of things, but 'upright' can describe an honest person.

heads.title: Pendency
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Its adjectives describe hanging or projecting physical states, or dependence as a situation rather than a character.

heads.title: Exteriority
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly external position; 'superficial' can describe a shallow person, and 'eccentric' a person's habitual oddity.

heads.title: Circumjacence
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Its adjectives describe surrounding position, with no application to character.

heads.title: Sinistrality
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Handedness words; 'sinister' can describe a menacing-seeming person, but this is marginal.

heads.title: Straightness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly geometric straightness; 'straight' in the sense of honest can describe a person's character.

heads.title: Flatness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Surface flatness adjectives; 'even' in its sense here is not about temper.

heads.title: Bluntness
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly dental or edge words; 'blunt' and 'bluff' describe a frank, abrupt manner in a person.

heads.title: Opening
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly physical openings; 'open' can describe a candid person.

heads.title: Closure
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly sealed or impassable states; 'tight' can describe a stingy person.

heads.title: Motion
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Mostly motion states; 'mercurial' and 'unquiet' can describe a person's temperament.

heads.title: Quiescence
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Several adjectives (quiet, unruffled, unmoved, stay-at-home, sedentary) can describe temperament or habit, but most describe physical stillness.

heads.title: Impulse
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Only 'impulsive' clearly describes a person's temperament; the rest concern motion or force.

heads.title: Direction
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: 'Straightforward', 'straight', 'direct' and 'unswerving' can describe an honest or steadfast person, but most words (directed, bound for, North) are spatial.

heads.title: Deviation
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: 'Devious', 'erratic', 'desultory' and 'vagrant' can describe a person's habits, while most words (circuitous, zigzag, crab-like) concern movement.

heads.title: Progression
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: 'Progressive' is at most an outlook, and 'advancing' and 'advanced' describe motion or stage, not character.

heads.title: Convergence
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Words such as converging, confluent, centripetal and asymptotic describe lines, paths or motion, never a person's character.

heads.title: Divergence
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Divergent, centrifugal and radiant describe motion or spread; 'aberrant' is the only word that could loosely describe a person.

heads.title: Shortcoming
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: Words like deficient, short, minus and out of depth describe lacks or situations, not a person's character.

heads.title: Agitation
heads.class_title: Words relating to space
heads.reason: 'Restless' and perhaps 'unquiet' describe temperament, while shaking, tremulous, convulsive and shambling describe physical agitation.

heads.title: Materiality
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Materialistic', 'impersonal' and 'unspiritual' can describe a person's outlook, but most words (bodily, corporeal, tangible) describe matter.

heads.title: Levity
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Airy', 'buoyant' and 'volatile' can describe a light-hearted or mercurial person, but most words describe physical lightness.

heads.title: Hardness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Stubborn', 'unbending', 'unyielding', 'inflexible', 'adamant' and 'rigid' routinely describe a person's firmness of character.

heads.title: Softness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Pliant', 'pliable', 'tractable', 'yielding' and 'soft' can describe a person's disposition, while most words (ductile, malleable, lithe) describe material or body.

heads.title: Elasticity
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Elastic', 'resilient' and 'buoyant' are mostly physical, though 'resilient' can describe a person's temperament.

heads.title: Tenacity
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Tenacious' and 'tough' can describe a person's character, while the rest (stringy, leathery, atomic) describe materials.

heads.title: Brittleness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Brash' and 'weak' can describe a person, while most words (frangible, fissile, splintery) describe breakable materials.

heads.title: Gaseity
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: All the words describe gases or vapours in this head's sense, so none describe a person.

heads.title: Dryness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Dryness words describe moisture or climate; 'dry' at most describes wit, and the rest are physical.

heads.title: Island
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Insular' can describe a narrow-minded person, while 'seagirt' describes an island's location.

heads.title: Organization
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Organized' might describe a methodical person, but organic and vacuolar describe biological matter.

heads.title: Life
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: 'Animated', 'full of life' and 'quick' can describe a lively person, but most words describe being alive or living matter.

heads.title: Killing
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mostly describes killing and violent acts, but blood thirsty, bloody minded, thuggish and murderous can describe a person's disposition.

heads.title: Agriculture
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Agricultural and rural words describe land and farming; only rustic can loosely describe a person's manner.

heads.title: Mankind
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Words such as human, mortal, national and civic describe kind or social relation, not a person's character.

heads.title: Man
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mainly describes sex and gender; manly and unwomanly can describe a person's qualities, but most words do not.

heads.title: Woman
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mainly describes sex and gender; ladylike, womanish and effeminate can describe a person's manner, but most words do not.

heads.title: Sexuality
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mostly describes sexual acts and things; passionate, hot-blooded, lusty, sensual and libidinous describe a person's temperament.

heads.title: Physical Insensibility
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mixes physical numbness (numb, comatose, palsied) with character words (callous, unfeeling, thick-skinned, hardened) that describe a person's disposition.

heads.title: Physical Pain
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: All words describe bodily pain or its state, not a person's character.

heads.title: Insipidity
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mostly describes taste and quality of things; bland, vapid, wishy-washy and mild can describe a person's temperament.

heads.title: Bitterness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Mainly describes taste; bitter, acerb and acerbic can describe a person's temperament or manner.

heads.title: Silence
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes silence and sound; only silent and solemn can loosely describe a person's habitual manner.

heads.title: Deafness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes lack of hearing and its states, not character.

heads.title: Dimness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes dim light, colour and appearance of things; none describes a person's character.

heads.title: Transparency
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes the transparency of things; serene is the only word that can describe a person's temperament.

heads.title: Opacity
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes opacity and murkiness of substances and air, not a person's character.

heads.title: Brown
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Colour words describing hair, skin or things; none describes character.

heads.title: Vision
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes the sense of sight and sharp eyesight, not character.

heads.title: Blindness
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes lack of sight, not character.

heads.title: Invisibility
heads.class_title: Words relating to matter
heads.reason: Describes being unseen or hidden; none describes a person's habitual character.

heads.title: Intellect
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.section: I. Operations of intellect in general
heads.reason: Describes intellectual faculties and mental operations rather than a person's temperament, though cerebral is close.

heads.title: Absence or want of Intellect
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.section: I. Operations of intellect in general
heads.reason: Mostly describes lack of intellect (void of reason, moronic, idiotic, brainless), but 'thoughtless' describes a habitual way of acting.

heads.title: Thought
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.section: I. Operations of intellect in general
heads.reason: Many adjectives describe settled temperament or habits of mind, such as thoughtful, sedate, introspective, contemplative, studious and philosophical.

heads.title: Incogitancy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.section: I. Operations of intellect in general
heads.reason: A few adjectives describe habitual manner (inconsiderate, thoughtless, unthinking), while most describe a momentary or intellectual state (vacant, diverted, unconsidered).

heads.title: Idea
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.section: I. Operations of intellect in general

heads.title: Topic
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.section: I. Operations of intellect in general
heads.reason: The adjectives describe what is currently in one's mind, not character.

heads.title: Curiosity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Inquisitive, prying, snoopy, nosy and overcurious are habitual traits a person can have.

heads.title: Incuriosity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Incurious, aloof, detached and indifferent are standing dispositions a person can have.

heads.title: Attention
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Attentive, observant and alert can describe a person, but most entries describe momentary states of absorption (rapt, transfixed, mesmerized).

heads.title: Inattention
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Many entries are habitual traits: heedless, scatter-brained, hare-brained, giddy-brained, bird-witted, offhand, unthinking.

heads.title: Care
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Careful, considerate, vigilant, watchful and guarded are character traits, but most entries describe a momentary state such as on guard, on watch or awake.

heads.title: Neglect
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Negligent, neglectful, careless, remiss, inconsiderate, unwary, imprudent and heedless are habitual ways a person can be.

heads.title: Inquiry
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe questions, inquiries and undecided matters rather than people.

heads.title: Answer
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe answers and responses, not a person's character.

heads.title: Experiment
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe tests and experiments, not people.

heads.title: Comparison
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe comparison relations between things.

heads.title: Incomparability
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe things that cannot be measured against each other.

heads.title: Discrimination
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe a faculty of discernment or distinctive features of things, not a person's character.

heads.title: Indiscrimination
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Only 'promiscuous' and perhaps 'indiscriminate' can describe a person's habits; the rest describe things or intellect.

heads.title: Identification
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties

heads.title: Measurement
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe measurability and perceptibility of things.

heads.title: Evidence
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe evidence and what it indicates.

heads.title: Counter Evidence
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The adjectives describe counter-evidence and the status of claims, not people.

heads.title: Qualification
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (qualifying, conditioned, restricted, conditional) describe statements and terms, not a person's character.

heads.title: Possibility
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (possible, feasible, attainable, within reach) describe things and outcomes, not people.

heads.title: Impossibility
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (impossible, insuperable, unattainable, absurd) describe schemes and circumstances; 'visionary' is the only near-character word and it is used of ideas here.

heads.title: Probability
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Mostly describes claims and evidence (plausible, specious, credible), though 'hopeful' can describe a person's disposition.

heads.title: Improbability
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (improbable, unheard of, inconceivable, far out) describe events and ideas; 'wild' and 'strange' are rarely character descriptions.

heads.title: Certainty
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Mostly describes things that are settled or proven (definite, unequivocal, inevitable), while 'positive' and 'decided' can describe a resolute person.

heads.title: Uncertainty
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Mixes things (doubtful, dubious, vague, ambiguous) with person-trait words such as 'indecisive' and 'undecided'.

heads.title: Reasoning
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Mostly describes arguments and debate, but 'argumentative', 'disputatious' and 'polemical' describe a person's habitual temperament.

heads.title: Intuition & Sophistry
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Mostly describes ideas and reasoning (unsound, invalid, illogical), though 'impulsive' and 'instinctive' can describe a person's habitual way of acting.

heads.title: Demonstration
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (demonstrable, conclusive, irrefutable, deducible) describe arguments and proofs, not people.

heads.title: Confutation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (refutable, defeasible, confuted) describe arguments and claims, not character.

heads.title: Judgment
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (judging, determinate, conclusive) describe acts of judgement or decisions rather than a person's character.

heads.title: Discovery
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties

heads.title: Misjudgment
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Most adjectives describe a person's habitual outlook: narrow-minded, prejudiced, intolerant, dogmatic, mean-spirited, fanatical.

heads.title: Overestimation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The only adjective, 'overestimated', describes a thing that has been overrated.

heads.title: Underestimation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (depreciated, unvalued) describe the value of things, not character.

heads.title: Belief
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: About half describe a person's disposition (cocksure, confident, confiding, unsuspicious), while the rest are states of mind or things.

heads.title: Unbelief. Doubt
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: About half describe a person's attitude (skeptical, suspicious, distrustful, shy), with the rest describing claims or things (incredible, questionable).

heads.title: Credulity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Nearly all describe a person's habitual naivety or gullibility (credulous, gullible, childish, superstitious).

heads.title: Incredulity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Nearly all describe a person's settled disposition to doubt (incredulous, cynical, distrustful, disposed to doubt).

heads.title: Assent
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Its adjectives (agreed, unanimous, uncontradicted, carried) describe agreement and votes, with only 'acquiescent' a character word.

heads.title: Dissent
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Mixed: 'intolerant' and perhaps 'sectarian' describe a person's disposition, while most others (dissenting, unconvinced, extorted, out of the question) describe opinions, beliefs or things.

heads.title: Knowledge
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Nearly all the adjectives describe a person's state of being informed or aware, such as 'au fait' or 'in the secret', not temperament; 'knowing' is at most marginal.

heads.title: Ignorance
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: These describe a person's lack of knowledge or education ('ignorant', 'untutored', 'unschooled') rather than how they habitually act.

heads.title: Scholar
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties

heads.title: Ignoramus
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: The sole adjective, 'shallow', describes a person's character in the sense of a shallow person.

heads.title: Truth
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: Most adjectives describe statements, facts or accuracy; only 'just' (fair-minded) clearly describes a person's character.

heads.title: Error
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: These describe statements, beliefs and things as wrong or untrue; 'false' in its deceitful sense is not the sense used here.

heads.title: Maxim
heads.class_title: Words relating to the intellectual faculties
heads.reason: All four describe sayings or maxims, not people.

heads.title: Absurdity

heads.title: Greed

heads.title: Prodigality

heads.title: Parsimony

heads.title: Inexcitability

heads.title: Pleasure

heads.title: Pain

heads.title: Discontent

heads.title: Regret

heads.title: Relief

heads.title: Aggravation

heads.title: Cheerfulness

heads.title: Dejection

heads.title: Rejoicing

heads.title: Lamentation

heads.title: Weariness

heads.title: Wit

heads.title: Ugliness

heads.title: Jewelry

heads.title: Simplicity

heads.title: Taste
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Vulgarity

heads.title: Fashion

heads.title: Ridiculousness

heads.title: Ridicule

heads.title: Courtesy

heads.title: Sullenness

heads.reason: Adjectives such as intemperate, licentious, debauched, self-indulgent and pampered describe a person's habitual conduct.

heads.title: Sensualist
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Asceticism
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Adjectives such as ascetic, austere, puritanical and cynical describe a person's habitual temperament.

heads.title: Fasting
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The adjectives (lenten, starved, half-starved, fasting) describe a state of abstinence or hunger, not character.

heads.title: Gluttony
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Gluttonous, greedy, gormandizing and swinish describe habitual character, while pampered, overfed and omnivorous describe condition or diet, so most adjectives qualify.

heads.title: Sobriety
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Sober and 'sober as a judge' mainly describe not being drunk, though a sober person can also mean a habitually serious or temperate temperament.

heads.title: Drunkenness
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The adjectives are almost all temporary states of intoxication, such as tipsy, bombed and groggy, rather than settled character.

heads.title: Purity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Most adjectives (pure, modest, decent, decorous, chaste, continent, virtuous, honest) describe a person's moral character.

heads.title: Impurity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Many adjectives (immodest, shameless, indecorous, indelicate, loose, coarse, ribald, concupiscent) describe a person's habitual conduct or disposition, though several describe speech or things.

heads.title: Libertine
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Legality
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Legal, legitimate, statutory, chartered and similar words describe laws, rights and institutions, not people.

heads.title: Illegality
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Only lawless, arbitrary, despotic, corrupt and irresponsible describe a person's character; the rest describe acts, rules or things.

heads.title: Jurisdiction
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Executive, judicial, municipal and similar adjectives describe authority, courts and institutions rather than people.

heads.title: Tribunal
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The only adjective, appellate, describes a court.

heads.title: Judge
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Lawyer
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Learned in the law, at the bar, forensic and esquire describe a lawyer's status or professional sphere, not character.

heads.title: Lawsuit
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The only adjective, qui tam, describes a type of legal action.

heads.title: Acquittal
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Acquitted, not guilty, not liable and similar words describe legal outcomes or status, not character.

heads.title: Condemnation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Guilty, condemned and self-convicted describe a legal or moral standing at a moment, and condemnatory describes a verdict, not a settled character.

heads.title: Punishment
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Punishing, penal, punitive and castigatory describe acts or systems of punishment, not a person's character.

heads.title: Reward
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Remunerative, compensatory, retributive and rewarding describe payments or outcomes, not people.

heads.title: Penalty
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Scourge
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Deity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Almighty, sacred, divine, omniscient and similar adjectives describe deities or sacred things, with only holy or spiritual occasionally describing a person.

heads.title: Angel
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Angelic, seraphic, cherubic and saintly describe a person's gentle, virtuous disposition.

heads.title: Satan
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Satanic, diabolic and devilish readily describe a person's malevolent character, and infernal can do so too.

heads.title: Jupiter
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The adjectives (god-like, fairy-like, sylph-like) describe beings or physical grace rather than a person's temperament.

heads.title: Demon
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Mostly describes supernatural things, but impish and fiendish can describe a person's mischievous or cruel disposition.

heads.title: Heaven
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The adjectives describe heaven and its qualities (celestial, paradisiacal, elysian), with only a stretched use of heavenly for a person.

heads.title: Hell
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Hellish, infernal and stygian describe places and things, not a person's character.

heads.title: Theology
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Theological and denominational describe doctrine and church affiliation; only religious can describe a person's habitual devotion.

heads.title: Orthodoxy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Mostly describes doctrine and belief, though faithful (loyal) is a character trait and orthodox can describe a person's views.

heads.title: Heterodoxy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Mixes belief and affiliation words (heretical, schismatic, pagan) with person-describing ones like iconoclastic and dissident, which denote a habitual nonconforming disposition.

heads.title: Judeo-Christian Revelation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Describes revelation, scripture and church texts (biblical, canonical, apocalyptic), not people.

heads.title: Pseudo-Revelation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Piety
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Nearly all adjectives (pious, devout, humble, saintly, reverent, godly) describe a person's habitual moral and religious character.

heads.title: Impiety
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Most adjectives (impious, profane, sanctimonious, unctuous, bigoted, fanatical, reprobate) describe a person's habitual attitude or disposition.

heads.title: Irreligion
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Most adjectives (godless, graceless, worldly, skeptical, freethinking, faithless) describe a person's habitual outlook or nature.

heads.title: Worship
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Mostly describes acts of worship; only devout and reverent clearly describe a person's disposition.

heads.title: Idolatry
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: The single adjective idolatrous describes a religious practice rather than a person's temperament.

heads.title: Sorcery
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Magic, mystic, talismanic and similar words describe practices and objects, not character.

heads.title: Spell
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Sorcerer
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Churchdom
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Describes church offices, government and institutions (prelatical, papal, episcopal), not personal character.

heads.title: Clergy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Consists of titles and ordination status (the Reverend, ordained, in orders), not character.

heads.title: Laity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Describes status or sphere (lay, civil, temporal, secular) rather than a person's disposition.

heads.title: Rite
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Describes rites and ceremonies (ritual, baptismal, paschal), not people.

heads.title: Canonicals
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Temple
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Describes monastic buildings and enclosed living (cloistered, conventual), a situation rather than character.
